industry.demand: Coal is ~75% of India's power generation (CARE, Apr-2026); coal's share of generation fell from ~71% in FY25 to ~68% in FY26 while renewables rose from ~22% to ~26% (ICICI Direct, 30-Jul-2026). Thermal generation rose 9.9% in Apr-Aug 2026 and power-plant coal stocks fell to ~23 MT (~8 days) by early September (Equirus via Business Today, 10-Sep-2026).
industry.supply: Captive and commercial mines produced 210.5 MT in FY26 (+10%, vs 191.0 MT in FY25) and take a growing share of incremental output (CARE; ICICI Direct). Coal India produced 768 MT (-1.6%) and sold 745 MT (-2.4%) in FY26.
industry.pricing: FSA (notified) prices are set by Coal India with an eye on the Government and power tariffs; no general notified-price increase was announced between FY26 and 30-Sep-2026 (BCCL's WPI-linked coking-coal revision of +0.24% from Apr-2026). E-auction premiums over notified prices: 228% (PL basis, FY23), 99% (FY24), 69% (FY25), 57% (FY26); 36% in Q4FY26, ~47% in Q1FY27, 43% average Apr-Jul 2026 (Chairman, AGM).
industry.policy: GST on coal raised to 18% from 5% and the Rs400/t compensation cess abolished from 22-Sep-2025 (CARE). Supreme Court allowed states to tax mineral rights retrospectively (Coal India's estimate: Rs31,591 cr gross, ~Rs6,000 cr net). Middle-East conflict raised diesel costs in 2026; Coal India chose to absorb them rather than raise prices (Kotak Neo, Apr-2026).

moat.scale: Near-monopoly (~74-80% of domestic output), ~49% of proven reserves, low-cost open-cast mines (97% of output) and ~618 MTPA of power linkages.
moat.pricing: Weak: notified prices are effectively policy-set (no general notified-price increase announced from Apr-2025 to 30-Sep-2026 in our sources; 2026 diesel costs absorbed), so Coal India cannot pass on wage and diesel inflation at will. Market pricing exists only in e-auctions (11-13% of volume).
moat.threats: Captive/commercial mines (+10% in FY26), renewables (coal's share of generation down ~3 points in FY26), high-cost legacy subsidiaries (BCCL, ECL) and a large, unionised workforce.
moat.verdict: A scale-and-reserves franchise without pricing power: it earns a high ROE because the asset base is old and the State lets it, not because it can raise prices. Moat: narrow.
